response: Normally sighted and visually impaired pedestrians can make accurate and reliable street crossing decisions. However, blind pedestrians may have difficulty making these decisions, particularly when relying solely on auditory information. They tend to overestimate vehicular gap times, which can lead to inaccurate and unreliable street crossing decisions. As a result, blind pedestrians may benefit from training to improve their detection ability and interpretation of vehicular gap times, enhancing their safety when crossing streets.
